authority: Derived navigation and observation projection. Completed accepted modules and the assembled accepted codebase own implemented behavior at the exact accepted revision. The atlas owns intended requirements and task predicates; completion needs separate admitted proof, unavailable in this tooling. Its active testing standard adds user-directed qualification requirements; the catalogue owns anchor/path mappings; retained receipts own their stated observations.

clusters.title: Task ownership and recovery
clusters.benefit: One durable ownership/budget/repair authority; crash and duplicate-work failures share one transaction boundary.
clusters.test: Restart and competing-attempt schedules preserve ownership, cost and unresolved obligations.

clusters.title: Worker routing and capability
clusters.benefit: Task-aware policy composes with maintained provider/agent runtimes.
clusters.test: Two real adapter types return effective identity, usage, limitations and cancellation.

clusters.title: Thread context and cohesion
clusters.benefit: Durable bounded briefs and actionable feedback connect specialists without transcript broadcast.
clusters.test: Obsolete briefs, missing acknowledgements and conflicting ownership cannot masquerade as progress.

clusters.title: Verification and numerical evidence
clusters.benefit: Actual candidate checks and Julia outcome analysis improve choices while preserving separate authority.
clusters.test: False completion and misleading numerical reports fail closed against independent fixtures.

clusters.title: Habitat operation and presentation
clusters.benefit: Herdr visibility and established lifecycle ownership expose useful state without an LLM status interpreter.
clusters.test: Pane reconnect, stalled services and control denial preserve task truth.

clusters.title: Application assembly
clusters.benefit: One composition root assembles narrow modules; dependency direction remains visible.
clusters.test: Packaged full-stack loop reaches accepted completion and delivery with the intended adapters.

modules.owns: Boundary data types, identities, errors and schema versions

tasks.intent: Define the first task and release contract
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T01 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: A real contained development task names inputs, acceptance, privacy, budget mode, pilot workload/window and measurable release targets. It can be expressed without an LLM or an inherited HEE packet set. Define loop limits, no-progress policy, criterion-to-verifier mapping and the minimal completion predicate before dispatch. Fix the initial module responsibilities, bidirectional boundary contracts and API/Unix-socket schema, with one state owner and no circular build dependencies. Freeze the minimal action IDs/envelope, error taxonomy, idempotency selector and state dimensions before the early CLI/UDS slice. Declare actual numeric resource/transport bounds during contract implementation.

tasks.intent: Qualify the narrow Rust-to-Pi adapter
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T02 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Fixture and later permitted smoke cases cover LF framing, model readback, usage, queued work, retry/end/settled ordering, cancellation and malformed/truncated records. Record the supported Rust/Pi protocol pair; no broad framework scaffold.

tasks.intent: Define common worker and plain inference contracts
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T03 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Launch, observe, cancel and result semantics work for tool-capable and output-only models. Missing features return unsupported; normalisation retains provider-specific usage and actual identity.

tasks.intent: Implement the transactional task ledger
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T04 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Submission replay is idempotent; same key with different content conflicts; task/attempt/event updates commit together; migrations and consistent backup have failure tests. The first ledger includes atomic conservative work/verification reservations, effect uncertainty and cancellation intent. task.get can recover a lost admission reply by principal-scoped request key. Allocate event identity before immutable manifest creation; acceptance commits its reference with the outbox. Publish immutable artifacts crash-durably under a declared filesystem contract before committing their SQLite references; a completed write alone is insufficient. Use file/metadata synchronisation and atomic publication as required by that contract. Historical acceptance and current evidence availability are separate facts.

tasks.intent: Build the model and agent roster
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T05 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Profiles and instances are distinct; declared/effective capabilities and freshness are visible; disable prevents new work; importing a roster starts nothing; secrets remain references. SQLite owns admitted roster revisions. Reviewed TOML manifests are explicit bootstrap/import/export inputs through the same validated update authority: expected-absent creates, expected-revision updates. Invalid or stale import changes nothing. Test update/disable, restart and stale re-import; no admitted mutation is lost and disabled records remain disabled. Active attempts retain their pinned record snapshots.

tasks.intent: Close one execute–verify–repair loop with completion evidence
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T06 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: A contained task uses the selected recipe and owned workspace, produces an artifact, runs an actual acceptance check and records result/cost. Worker end or exit zero alone cannot accept it. A failing candidate is repaired and reverified; exhausted and verifier-error cases stop truthfully. Acceptance and completion outbox event commit together with a criterion-to-evidence manifest bound to the actual candidate. Even this first loop requires a safe minimal budget gate and reserved verification allocation; unknown accounting cannot satisfy a hard ceiling. Rich cross-adapter reconciliation follows in T10. Terminal cancellation requires observed cleanup/effect reconciliation.

tasks.intent: Recover and cancel owned attempts
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T07 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Crashes before/after dispatch acknowledgement, stale generations, PID reuse, queued Pi messages and partial cleanup produce correct recoverable states without duplicate writes. Ambiguous external outcomes remain explicit. Cover restart at verification/evidence/acceptance boundaries; lease expiry alone cannot authorize reuse of a still-writable old workspace. Acceptance explicitly rejects any earlier committed cancellation intent, even before terminal cleanup. If acceptance committed first, later cancellation cannot rewrite history. Startup may reattach observation to a positively reconciled live attempt without redispatch. Restored ledger epochs cannot silently reuse prior event cursors.

tasks.intent: Add a second worker adapter
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T08 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: A selected native harness or plain inference backend passes the common contract; actual supported model/effort is recorded. No success inferred from terminal prose. Version-specific limitations are listed.

tasks.intent: Implement deterministic eligibility and routing
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T09 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Capability/context/privacy/availability constraints exclude invalid recipes; rules choose a valid recipe with stable explanation; ties and insufficient evidence use an explicit baseline; routing itself makes zero model calls.

tasks.intent: Account for whole-task cost and bounded fallback
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T10 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Concurrent reservations cannot exceed configured bounds; retries/checking/compaction are included; unknown usage is visible; hard-ceiling tasks reject incompatible accounting; fallback cannot cross privacy or tool constraints.

tasks.intent: Minimise repeated context and noisy supervision
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T11 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Context is bounded to task needs; actionable wakes are deduplicated/batched; controlled idle and repeated unchanged events cause zero model requests; summaries and compaction usage are accounted for. Context records distinguish required source-file coverage from task-critical call/dependency/ownership relationship coverage. Expose each gap and account for discovery, supplemental reads and repeated context as well as final packet size.

tasks.intent: Build inspect-only service inventory and useful probes
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T13 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Daemon, one-shot, library, remote endpoint and neural-operator records use appropriate observations. Unknown/stale readiness cannot become healthy; discovery claims no lifecycle ownership. Apply T05 admitted-revision and explicit import/export rules to service records. Test service update/disable, restart and stale/invalid import; observed inventory cannot overwrite effective authority or grant lifecycle control.

tasks.intent: Add scoped lifecycle actions through systemd
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T14 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Only explicitly managed units can change state; dependencies and result readback are checked; stalled service, restart loop and coordinator restart cases do not create competing process owners.

tasks.intent: Expose the task and roster views in Herdr
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T16 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Task cards show owner, model, state, spend and outcome; pane closure does not erase task state; reconnect resynchronises; event gap/poll fallback and user cancel are exercised on the actual public Herdr API. Display the current loop iteration, failing criterion, remaining budget, completion evidence and notification state. The captured Herdr protocol has live events without durable replay cursors. Qualify resubscription and coherent snapshot reconciliation; do not claim gap-free Herdr history.

tasks.intent: Exercise the critical failure matrix
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T17 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Lost completion, stalled runtime, stale lease, duplicate submission, exhausted budget, provider failure and disk error each hit the intended boundary. Record exact build/config and limitations; do not substitute test count for outcome. Fabricated done, wrong-subject evidence, mid-check artifact mutation, broken verifier, repeated non-progress, failed parent integration and lost final notification cannot produce false accepted completion. Exercise partial/coalesced frames, slow API readers, stale event cursors, wrong socket/session and lost response after effect. Inject failures between artifact write, durability publication and acceptance commit under the declared filesystem contract. Missing, expired or corrupt evidence at later readback must report current unavailability while preserving the historical event; no fresh verification may be inferred. Fault experiments distinguish invalid fixtures, excluded cells and unmeasured gates. A formatting rejection that prevents the intended behavioral fault does not prove that behavioral detector works.

tasks.intent: Package and prove backup, upgrade and rollback
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T18 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Versioned artifact, dependencies and config are identifiable; login/reboot behaviour is observed; consistent backup restores tasks/artifacts; upgrade and schema-compatible rollback run on disposable state before installation. Before restoring a pre-upgrade database, preserve the failed/current ledger and reconcile post-backup operations, effects and usage. Use a disposable bounded qualification domain; a changed event epoch alone does not prevent replaying external effects erased by restore. Backup/restore and retention must preserve declared durability and unresolved evidence obligations. Retention policy states which accepted proof must remain retrievable; evidence loss is reported rather than silently rewriting acceptance or claiming current proof. Integration freshness reports include source additions/removals/changes; accepting an updated baseline is a separate versioned reconciliation, never an automatic consequence of discovery. Restore qualification compares the expected content/service inventory, includes an omitted-service control and independently reads back answering interfaces and residual processes in the disposable scope. File copying alone cannot prove restored operation; local recovery does not establish off-site disaster recovery.

tasks.intent: Run the constrained real-work pilot
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T19 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Under the concrete commissioning choice D07, run the Phase-1 workload/window; measure accepted work, total cost, rework, idle calls and incidents. Meet declared release targets or fix the observed gap without widening scope. Audit sampled criterion-to-evidence records and real repair loops; report false acceptance, verification error and completion-delivery failures.

tasks.intent: Release the scoped product and prune unnecessary machinery
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T20 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: A fresh operator can submit, inspect, cancel, recover and manage the declared services. Publish supported versions/limits and actual evidence. Remove duplicate status/procedure sources; advanced roadmap items remain optional. Pruning/update review keeps observed drift separate from the accepted baseline. Exact source anchors support presence/location claims only, not runtime behavior or compatibility.

tasks.intent: Implement the bounded Rust–Julia analysis exchange
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T21 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: An immutable attempt dataset produces a reproducible Julia report with dataset/schema identity. Missing data, nonfinite values, stale results, timeout and cancellation are explicit. Julia failure preserves the approved route and cannot mutate task ownership. Exercise the bidirectional contract corpus with independent expectations, numeric tolerances and explicit Julia bounds checks.

tasks.intent: Add bounded cohorts and measurable cohesion
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T22 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Roles share a versioned objective, distinct artifact ownership and bounded messages. Cross-agent resource conflicts and stale-generation callbacks are rejected. Compare one-worker and specialist-cohort outcomes including cost, errors, disagreement and rework; idle cohorts stop. Persist logical thread identity, versioned mailbox obligations and parent join requirements; protect shared interface/lockfile ownership and recover orchestrator loss without duplicate dispatch. Enforce one conserved parent/child allocation tree. Waiting parents release resources children require. Semantic cross-module calls remain mediated by the composition root and current action authority. Thread briefs preserve the task-critical relationships needed by the receiving specialist; a list of included files alone cannot prove adequate context. Narrow the question explicitly when required coverage exceeds its bound.

tasks.intent: Qualify a PyTorch-compatible numerical worker only when justified
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T23 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Compare Julia-native execution with a selected tch/LibTorch or external model-service path on the same model/data. Record language boundary, versions, device, operator support, memory/copy/startup cost and cancellation. A reject/defer decision is a valid outcome; no mandatory Python product code.

tasks.intent: Establish the Rust and Julia quality contract
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T25 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Pinned format/lint/test recipes include pedantic Clippy, supported feature profiles, Rust doctests, locked Julia tests with explicit bounds checks, and honest case/skip counts. A deliberately bad fixture fails for the intended reason. Checks grow with each vertical slice; no blanket lint suppression. The verifier recipe separates trusted launch/collection from candidate-controlled compiler/build/test processes. Captured process exit status is an observation; candidate structured reports remain claims requiring recipe checks and independent expectations. Early trusted-host fixture tests must disclose that stronger hostile-code containment is not yet qualified. Qualify consequential gate discrimination on a passing baseline and an independently justified fault with the intended failure reason; include benign near-neighbors where false positives matter. Non-blocking authoring hooks do not satisfy required release gates.

tasks.intent: Define the threat model and security review contract
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T26 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Map task authority, context provenance, credentials, IPC, same-UID limits, isolation and trusted verifier ownership. Assign bounded negative cases and finding disposition. Confirm the selected security-model capability without granting extra execution authority. Include candidate-controlled build scripts, procedural macros, test binaries and Julia package hooks in the threat model; invoking them via a trusted verifier confers no collector authority.

tasks.intent: Close security findings against the integrated release
tasks.route: Security + verification threads, separate from finding implementer
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T27 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Reproduce material findings, verify fixes and residual dispositions on the actual packaged candidate. Prompt injection, credential exposure, socket/method misuse, stale writers, fabricated evidence, dependency drift and resource exhaustion cannot produce false acceptance. Model review alone is not closure. In disposable qualified fixtures, candidate build/test code attempts to alter protected fixture, evidence and control paths. The boundary must refuse the effect and the independent collector must expose the attempt; an exit-zero candidate report cannot certify its own integrity. Security fault cases require a valid unmutated baseline and the intended observable refusal. Preserve unmeasured/excluded scope; one corpus with no unique catch does not justify removing a gate.

tasks.intent: Expose one authoritative action catalogue to CLI, API and LLM tools
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T28 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: One action definition drives CLI/Unix schemas and one selected LLM-tool adapter. Bounded discovery/inspection/preview, scoped invocation, identity/idempotency and evidence readback work end to end. Denial remains denial across transports; untrusted workers receive no operator socket; generated projections cannot drift. task.get and analysis.get support their own principal-scoped admission-key readback; service.inspect can query the lifecycle operation key without confusing current health with historic effect. events.subscribe without a cursor provides a bounded coherent bootstrap snapshot plus high-water cursor. Distinguish request correlation from durable idempotency. Base Pi RPC does not supply the engine tool callback path; qualify the actual inherited channel or maintained bridge. Template-produced requests preserve literal typed values at the action boundary; model-emitted risk or approval fields never confer effect authority.

tasks.intent: Qualify modular Bash, Pi, skill and workflow integration packages
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T29 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Thin updatable packages share action/procedure identity and preserve authority, arguments, producer exit status, cancellation and evidence. Pi errors/parallel calls/reload and effective tool-set readback are qualified; skills disclose bounded context. Two typed compositions close their real return paths. Version switching preserves active attempts and rollback; no separate scheduler or silent self-update. Keep the admitted package/protocol tuple pinned through every active attempt. Revoked/reloaded tool handlers cannot retain effect authority. No custom Pi-host glue is selected until its concrete packaging need is established. Each integration renders its owned template once, then passes literal typed data rather than copying/re-templating procedure bodies. Focused fixtures include braces, quotes, newlines, dollar signs and leading dashes, with exact final argv/JSON and producer-status checks. Preserve source and relationship coverage with whole-workflow context accounting. Source-change reports cannot advance accepted compatibility/source baselines.

modules.reference_limits: Authentication, complete public schemas, canonical cross-language encodings and hostile collector custody remain production qualifications.

profile.surface: Rust types and validation facade shared by declared consumers; serializable boundary schemas through existing APIs.

operations.inputs: Schema version; task, attempt, generation, caller and correlation identities; bounded payload

operations.outputs: Stable discriminated result preserving denied, failed, cancelled and unknown distinctions

operations.inputs: Producer/consumer version and declared capabilities
operations.outputs: Supported subset or explicit incompatibility

profile.errors_and_limits: Bound lengths, integer ranges and enum variants; reject missing identity and ambiguous encodings before effects. Unknown versions are not guessed.
profile.effects_and_concurrency: Pure constructors/validation. No database, grants, process control or state acceptance. Changes propagate to all wire consumers through explicit compatibility review.
profile.required_proof: Round-trip and malformed schema cases; old/new consumer fixtures; non-lossy error and identity projection; fuzz/property campaign on parsing bounds.

profile.outcome: Typed request/result/error and identity/version contracts round-trip without losing semantics across declared consumers.
profile.integrated_scenario: Send a valid versioned request through two declared consumer projections and compare typed identity, errors and cancellation fields.
profile.fault_and_benign: Reject oversized/malformed or incompatible payload before allocation/dispatch; accept the bounded compatible counterpart.
profile.complexity_boundary: No registry, transport listener or task scheduler in the contract library.

profile.focus: Untrusted schema/frame bounds, compatibility, identity preservation and parser fuzz controls.
profile.fault_and_benign: Reject oversized/malformed or incompatible payload before allocation/dispatch; accept the bounded compatible counterpart.

limitations: Record consistency is not producer authentication, runtime certification or task acceptance.

tasks.intent: Define the first task and release contract
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T01 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: A real contained development task names inputs, acceptance, privacy, budget mode, pilot workload/window and measurable release targets. It can be expressed without an LLM or an inherited HEE packet set. Define loop limits, no-progress policy, criterion-to-verifier mapping and the minimal completion predicate before dispatch. Fix the initial module responsibilities, bidirectional boundary contracts and API/Unix-socket schema, with one state owner and no circular build dependencies. Freeze the minimal action IDs/envelope, error taxonomy, idempotency selector and state dimensions before the early CLI/UDS slice. Declare actual numeric resource/transport bounds during contract implementation.

tasks.intent: Implement the transactional task ledger
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T04 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Submission replay is idempotent; same key with different content conflicts; task/attempt/event updates commit together; migrations and consistent backup have failure tests. The first ledger includes atomic conservative work/verification reservations, effect uncertainty and cancellation intent. task.get can recover a lost admission reply by principal-scoped request key. Allocate event identity before immutable manifest creation; acceptance commits its reference with the outbox. Publish immutable artifacts crash-durably under a declared filesystem contract before committing their SQLite references; a completed write alone is insufficient. Use file/metadata synchronisation and atomic publication as required by that contract. Historical acceptance and current evidence availability are separate facts.

tasks.intent: Close one execute–verify–repair loop with completion evidence
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T06 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: A contained task uses the selected recipe and owned workspace, produces an artifact, runs an actual acceptance check and records result/cost. Worker end or exit zero alone cannot accept it. A failing candidate is repaired and reverified; exhausted and verifier-error cases stop truthfully. Acceptance and completion outbox event commit together with a criterion-to-evidence manifest bound to the actual candidate. Even this first loop requires a safe minimal budget gate and reserved verification allocation; unknown accounting cannot satisfy a hard ceiling. Rich cross-adapter reconciliation follows in T10. Terminal cancellation requires observed cleanup/effect reconciliation.

tasks.intent: Recover and cancel owned attempts
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T07 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Crashes before/after dispatch acknowledgement, stale generations, PID reuse, queued Pi messages and partial cleanup produce correct recoverable states without duplicate writes. Ambiguous external outcomes remain explicit. Cover restart at verification/evidence/acceptance boundaries; lease expiry alone cannot authorize reuse of a still-writable old workspace. Acceptance explicitly rejects any earlier committed cancellation intent, even before terminal cleanup. If acceptance committed first, later cancellation cannot rewrite history. Startup may reattach observation to a positively reconciled live attempt without redispatch. Restored ledger epochs cannot silently reuse prior event cursors.

tasks.intent: Account for whole-task cost and bounded fallback
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T10 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Concurrent reservations cannot exceed configured bounds; retries/checking/compaction are included; unknown usage is visible; hard-ceiling tasks reject incompatible accounting; fallback cannot cross privacy or tool constraints.

tasks.intent: Compare routing against a fixed-model baseline
tasks.route: Julia evaluation engineer + independent task reviewer
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T12 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Held-out representative tasks use the same acceptance method; failed/abandoned attempts enter cost totals; report uncertainty by class and review work. Retain a simple policy unless a challenger improves the declared tradeoff. Julia reports routing and cohort comparisons from the same immutable outcomes, with uncertainty and missingness. Include failed, cancelled and abandoned attempts and unknown usage at an explicit dataset cutoff; disclose exclusion and censoring policy.

tasks.intent: Add scoped lifecycle actions through systemd
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T14 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Only explicitly managed units can change state; dependencies and result readback are checked; stalled service, restart loop and coordinator restart cases do not create competing process owners.

tasks.intent: Exercise the critical failure matrix
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T17 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Lost completion, stalled runtime, stale lease, duplicate submission, exhausted budget, provider failure and disk error each hit the intended boundary. Record exact build/config and limitations; do not substitute test count for outcome. Fabricated done, wrong-subject evidence, mid-check artifact mutation, broken verifier, repeated non-progress, failed parent integration and lost final notification cannot produce false accepted completion. Exercise partial/coalesced frames, slow API readers, stale event cursors, wrong socket/session and lost response after effect. Inject failures between artifact write, durability publication and acceptance commit under the declared filesystem contract. Missing, expired or corrupt evidence at later readback must report current unavailability while preserving the historical event; no fresh verification may be inferred. Fault experiments distinguish invalid fixtures, excluded cells and unmeasured gates. A formatting rejection that prevents the intended behavioral fault does not prove that behavioral detector works.

tasks.intent: Package and prove backup, upgrade and rollback
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T18 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Versioned artifact, dependencies and config are identifiable; login/reboot behaviour is observed; consistent backup restores tasks/artifacts; upgrade and schema-compatible rollback run on disposable state before installation. Before restoring a pre-upgrade database, preserve the failed/current ledger and reconcile post-backup operations, effects and usage. Use a disposable bounded qualification domain; a changed event epoch alone does not prevent replaying external effects erased by restore. Backup/restore and retention must preserve declared durability and unresolved evidence obligations. Retention policy states which accepted proof must remain retrievable; evidence loss is reported rather than silently rewriting acceptance or claiming current proof. Integration freshness reports include source additions/removals/changes; accepting an updated baseline is a separate versioned reconciliation, never an automatic consequence of discovery. Restore qualification compares the expected content/service inventory, includes an omitted-service control and independently reads back answering interfaces and residual processes in the disposable scope. File copying alone cannot prove restored operation; local recovery does not establish off-site disaster recovery.

tasks.intent: Run the constrained real-work pilot
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T19 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Under the concrete commissioning choice D07, run the Phase-1 workload/window; measure accepted work, total cost, rework, idle calls and incidents. Meet declared release targets or fix the observed gap without widening scope. Audit sampled criterion-to-evidence records and real repair loops; report false acceptance, verification error and completion-delivery failures.

tasks.intent: Release the scoped product and prune unnecessary machinery
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T20 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: A fresh operator can submit, inspect, cancel, recover and manage the declared services. Publish supported versions/limits and actual evidence. Remove duplicate status/procedure sources; advanced roadmap items remain optional. Pruning/update review keeps observed drift separate from the accepted baseline. Exact source anchors support presence/location claims only, not runtime behavior or compatibility.

tasks.intent: Add bounded cohorts and measurable cohesion
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T22 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Roles share a versioned objective, distinct artifact ownership and bounded messages. Cross-agent resource conflicts and stale-generation callbacks are rejected. Compare one-worker and specialist-cohort outcomes including cost, errors, disagreement and rework; idle cohorts stop. Persist logical thread identity, versioned mailbox obligations and parent join requirements; protect shared interface/lockfile ownership and recover orchestrator loss without duplicate dispatch. Enforce one conserved parent/child allocation tree. Waiting parents release resources children require. Semantic cross-module calls remain mediated by the composition root and current action authority. Thread briefs preserve the task-critical relationships needed by the receiving specialist; a list of included files alone cannot prove adequate context. Narrow the question explicitly when required coverage exceeds its bound.

tasks.intent: Establish the Rust and Julia quality contract
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T25 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Pinned format/lint/test recipes include pedantic Clippy, supported feature profiles, Rust doctests, locked Julia tests with explicit bounds checks, and honest case/skip counts. A deliberately bad fixture fails for the intended reason. Checks grow with each vertical slice; no blanket lint suppression. The verifier recipe separates trusted launch/collection from candidate-controlled compiler/build/test processes. Captured process exit status is an observation; candidate structured reports remain claims requiring recipe checks and independent expectations. Early trusted-host fixture tests must disclose that stronger hostile-code containment is not yet qualified. Qualify consequential gate discrimination on a passing baseline and an independently justified fault with the intended failure reason; include benign near-neighbors where false positives matter. Non-blocking authoring hooks do not satisfy required release gates.

tasks.intent: Define the threat model and security review contract
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T26 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Map task authority, context provenance, credentials, IPC, same-UID limits, isolation and trusted verifier ownership. Assign bounded negative cases and finding disposition. Confirm the selected security-model capability without granting extra execution authority. Include candidate-controlled build scripts, procedural macros, test binaries and Julia package hooks in the threat model; invoking them via a trusted verifier confers no collector authority.

tasks.intent: Close security findings against the integrated release
tasks.route: Security + verification threads, separate from finding implementer
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T27 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Reproduce material findings, verify fixes and residual dispositions on the actual packaged candidate. Prompt injection, credential exposure, socket/method misuse, stale writers, fabricated evidence, dependency drift and resource exhaustion cannot produce false acceptance. Model review alone is not closure. In disposable qualified fixtures, candidate build/test code attempts to alter protected fixture, evidence and control paths. The boundary must refuse the effect and the independent collector must expose the attempt; an exit-zero candidate report cannot certify its own integrity. Security fault cases require a valid unmutated baseline and the intended observable refusal. Preserve unmeasured/excluded scope; one corpus with no unique catch does not justify removing a gate.

tasks.intent: Qualify modular Bash, Pi, skill and workflow integration packages
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T29 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Thin updatable packages share action/procedure identity and preserve authority, arguments, producer exit status, cancellation and evidence. Pi errors/parallel calls/reload and effective tool-set readback are qualified; skills disclose bounded context. Two typed compositions close their real return paths. Version switching preserves active attempts and rollback; no separate scheduler or silent self-update. Keep the admitted package/protocol tuple pinned through every active attempt. Revoked/reloaded tool handlers cannot retain effect authority. No custom Pi-host glue is selected until its concrete packaging need is established. Each integration renders its owned template once, then passes literal typed data rather than copying/re-templating procedure bodies. Focused fixtures include braces, quotes, newlines, dollar signs and leading dashes, with exact final argv/JSON and producer-status checks. Preserve source and relationship coverage with whole-workflow context accounting. Source-change reports cannot advance accepted compatibility/source baselines.

implementation_tasks.intent: Build the model and agent roster
implementation_tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T05 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
implementation_tasks.acceptance: Profiles and instances are distinct; declared/effective capabilities and freshness are visible; disable prevents new work; importing a roster starts nothing; secrets remain references. SQLite owns admitted roster revisions. Reviewed TOML manifests are explicit bootstrap/import/export inputs through the same validated update authority: expected-absent creates, expected-revision updates. Invalid or stale import changes nothing. Test update/disable, restart and stale re-import; no admitted mutation is lost and disabled records remain disabled. Active attempts retain their pinned record snapshots.

profile.surface: Rust task coordinator facade; operator and tool access exclusively through admitted actions and app transports.

operations.inputs: Caller capability, task specification, acceptance revision, limits and idempotency key
operations.outputs: Preview exclusions or durable task/attempt identity and initial state

operations.inputs: Task identity; bounded listing cursor or cancellation request
operations.outputs: Committed snapshot/page or acknowledged cancellation obligation

operations.inputs: Expected generation, observed worker/checker facts, explicit operator resolution authority
operations.outputs: Committed transition with evidence links or conflict/denial

profile.errors_and_limits: Bound task/attempt counts and deadlines. Refuse stale generations, incompatible retry bodies and missing grants. Cancellation acknowledgement is not process settlement.
profile.effects_and_concurrency: Owns the plan/execute/observe/verify/repair/close loop. Mutations commit through store with conservative budget and retained uncertainty; checker evidence alone does not grant acceptance.
profile.required_proof: Boundary acceptance, duplicate submission, lost reply/readback, stale result, verify-repair-verify loop, cancellation and exhausted-budget cases.

profile.outcome: One durable task lifecycle performs admit → execute → verify → repair/escalate → reverify → accept, with correct terminal and pending states.
profile.integrated_scenario: Submit once, lose the reply, read back the same task, repair a failed candidate and accept only the verified subject.
profile.fault_and_benign: Late result, cancellation/acceptance race and exhausted budget never create duplicate effects or false acceptance; valid current result can advance.
profile.complexity_boundary: Task state is not duplicated in adapters, panes or workflow packages.

profile.focus: Unauthorized state transitions, forged/stale acceptance, replay, cancellation/acceptance races and effect custody.
profile.fault_and_benign: Late result, cancellation/acceptance race and exhausted budget never create duplicate effects or false acceptance; valid current result can advance.

limitations: Record consistency is not producer authentication, runtime certification or task acceptance.

Future timestamps are unqualified; no age expiry or current deployment health is inferred.

tasks.intent: Implement the transactional task ledger
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T04 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Submission replay is idempotent; same key with different content conflicts; task/attempt/event updates commit together; migrations and consistent backup have failure tests. The first ledger includes atomic conservative work/verification reservations, effect uncertainty and cancellation intent. task.get can recover a lost admission reply by principal-scoped request key. Allocate event identity before immutable manifest creation; acceptance commits its reference with the outbox. Publish immutable artifacts crash-durably under a declared filesystem contract before committing their SQLite references; a completed write alone is insufficient. Use file/metadata synchronisation and atomic publication as required by that contract. Historical acceptance and current evidence availability are separate facts.

tasks.intent: Close one execute–verify–repair loop with completion evidence
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T06 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: A contained task uses the selected recipe and owned workspace, produces an artifact, runs an actual acceptance check and records result/cost. Worker end or exit zero alone cannot accept it. A failing candidate is repaired and reverified; exhausted and verifier-error cases stop truthfully. Acceptance and completion outbox event commit together with a criterion-to-evidence manifest bound to the actual candidate. Even this first loop requires a safe minimal budget gate and reserved verification allocation; unknown accounting cannot satisfy a hard ceiling. Rich cross-adapter reconciliation follows in T10. Terminal cancellation requires observed cleanup/effect reconciliation.

tasks.intent: Recover and cancel owned attempts
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T07 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Crashes before/after dispatch acknowledgement, stale generations, PID reuse, queued Pi messages and partial cleanup produce correct recoverable states without duplicate writes. Ambiguous external outcomes remain explicit. Cover restart at verification/evidence/acceptance boundaries; lease expiry alone cannot authorize reuse of a still-writable old workspace. Acceptance explicitly rejects any earlier committed cancellation intent, even before terminal cleanup. If acceptance committed first, later cancellation cannot rewrite history. Startup may reattach observation to a positively reconciled live attempt without redispatch. Restored ledger epochs cannot silently reuse prior event cursors.

tasks.intent: Add scoped lifecycle actions through systemd
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T14 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Only explicitly managed units can change state; dependencies and result readback are checked; stalled service, restart loop and coordinator restart cases do not create competing process owners.

tasks.intent: Qualify worker isolation and secret delivery
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T15 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Untrusted worker cannot read coordinator state/socket or unintended credentials; argv/env/cwd are explicit; resource and process-group cleanup are tested; trusted-host mode has an honest separate claim. Qualify isolation for candidate-controlled verification subprocesses, including build.rs, procedural macros, tests and Julia hooks. The trusted launcher/collector remains outside that execution domain; candidate code cannot modify protected fixtures, authoritative evidence, ledger/socket or unrelated secrets.

tasks.intent: Exercise the critical failure matrix
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T17 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Lost completion, stalled runtime, stale lease, duplicate submission, exhausted budget, provider failure and disk error each hit the intended boundary. Record exact build/config and limitations; do not substitute test count for outcome. Fabricated done, wrong-subject evidence, mid-check artifact mutation, broken verifier, repeated non-progress, failed parent integration and lost final notification cannot produce false accepted completion. Exercise partial/coalesced frames, slow API readers, stale event cursors, wrong socket/session and lost response after effect. Inject failures between artifact write, durability publication and acceptance commit under the declared filesystem contract. Missing, expired or corrupt evidence at later readback must report current unavailability while preserving the historical event; no fresh verification may be inferred. Fault experiments distinguish invalid fixtures, excluded cells and unmeasured gates. A formatting rejection that prevents the intended behavioral fault does not prove that behavioral detector works.

tasks.intent: Package and prove backup, upgrade and rollback
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T18 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Versioned artifact, dependencies and config are identifiable; login/reboot behaviour is observed; consistent backup restores tasks/artifacts; upgrade and schema-compatible rollback run on disposable state before installation. Before restoring a pre-upgrade database, preserve the failed/current ledger and reconcile post-backup operations, effects and usage. Use a disposable bounded qualification domain; a changed event epoch alone does not prevent replaying external effects erased by restore. Backup/restore and retention must preserve declared durability and unresolved evidence obligations. Retention policy states which accepted proof must remain retrievable; evidence loss is reported rather than silently rewriting acceptance or claiming current proof. Integration freshness reports include source additions/removals/changes; accepting an updated baseline is a separate versioned reconciliation, never an automatic consequence of discovery. Restore qualification compares the expected content/service inventory, includes an omitted-service control and independently reads back answering interfaces and residual processes in the disposable scope. File copying alone cannot prove restored operation; local recovery does not establish off-site disaster recovery.

tasks.intent: Run the constrained real-work pilot
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T19 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Under the concrete commissioning choice D07, run the Phase-1 workload/window; measure accepted work, total cost, rework, idle calls and incidents. Meet declared release targets or fix the observed gap without widening scope. Audit sampled criterion-to-evidence records and real repair loops; report false acceptance, verification error and completion-delivery failures.

tasks.intent: Release the scoped product and prune unnecessary machinery
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T20 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: A fresh operator can submit, inspect, cancel, recover and manage the declared services. Publish supported versions/limits and actual evidence. Remove duplicate status/procedure sources; advanced roadmap items remain optional. Pruning/update review keeps observed drift separate from the accepted baseline. Exact source anchors support presence/location claims only, not runtime behavior or compatibility.

tasks.intent: Establish the Rust and Julia quality contract
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T25 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Pinned format/lint/test recipes include pedantic Clippy, supported feature profiles, Rust doctests, locked Julia tests with explicit bounds checks, and honest case/skip counts. A deliberately bad fixture fails for the intended reason. Checks grow with each vertical slice; no blanket lint suppression. The verifier recipe separates trusted launch/collection from candidate-controlled compiler/build/test processes. Captured process exit status is an observation; candidate structured reports remain claims requiring recipe checks and independent expectations. Early trusted-host fixture tests must disclose that stronger hostile-code containment is not yet qualified. Qualify consequential gate discrimination on a passing baseline and an independently justified fault with the intended failure reason; include benign near-neighbors where false positives matter. Non-blocking authoring hooks do not satisfy required release gates.

tasks.intent: Define the threat model and security review contract
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T26 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Map task authority, context provenance, credentials, IPC, same-UID limits, isolation and trusted verifier ownership. Assign bounded negative cases and finding disposition. Confirm the selected security-model capability without granting extra execution authority. Include candidate-controlled build scripts, procedural macros, test binaries and Julia package hooks in the threat model; invoking them via a trusted verifier confers no collector authority.

tasks.intent: Close security findings against the integrated release
tasks.route: Security + verification threads, separate from finding implementer
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T27 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Reproduce material findings, verify fixes and residual dispositions on the actual packaged candidate. Prompt injection, credential exposure, socket/method misuse, stale writers, fabricated evidence, dependency drift and resource exhaustion cannot produce false acceptance. Model review alone is not closure. In disposable qualified fixtures, candidate build/test code attempts to alter protected fixture, evidence and control paths. The boundary must refuse the effect and the independent collector must expose the attempt; an exit-zero candidate report cannot certify its own integrity. Security fault cases require a valid unmutated baseline and the intended observable refusal. Preserve unmeasured/excluded scope; one corpus with no unique catch does not justify removing a gate.

implementation_tasks.intent: Build the model and agent roster
implementation_tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T05 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
implementation_tasks.acceptance: Profiles and instances are distinct; declared/effective capabilities and freshness are visible; disable prevents new work; importing a roster starts nothing; secrets remain references. SQLite owns admitted roster revisions. Reviewed TOML manifests are explicit bootstrap/import/export inputs through the same validated update authority: expected-absent creates, expected-revision updates. Invalid or stale import changes nothing. Test update/disable, restart and stale re-import; no admitted mutation is lost and disabled records remain disabled. Active attempts retain their pinned record snapshots.

implementation_tasks.intent: Build inspect-only service inventory and useful probes
implementation_tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T13 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
implementation_tasks.acceptance: Daemon, one-shot, library, remote endpoint and neural-operator records use appropriate observations. Unknown/stale readiness cannot become healthy; discovery claims no lifecycle ownership. Apply T05 admitted-revision and explicit import/export rules to service records. Test service update/disable, restart and stale/invalid import; observed inventory cannot overwrite effective authority or grant lifecycle control.

modules.reference_limits: Reopen and injected SQL abort are exercised. Power-cut behavior, disk-full uncertainty, adversarial path custody, retention, restore and multi-resource admission remain unqualified.

modules.reference_limits:
A live Pi/native adapter, complete stream grammar, one retry owner, scope cancellation, accounting and provider compatibility still need qualification.

### Native adapter — version-specific limitations (recorded 2026-09-21, T08 contract-integration release 1f2b847c…, actual reviews 8d274802…/ef2ea679…)

profile.surface: Rust adapter facade over bounded Pi/native/inference protocols; no access to the operator control socket by default.

operations.inputs: Attempt/generation, exact recipe, scoped workspace, limits, credentials and cancellation channel

profile.errors_and_limits: Frame/stream/size/time bounds and schema negotiation; malformed, duplicated, stale or spoofed messages cannot close a task.
profile.effects_and_concurrency: One adapter owns its process lifecycle under coordinator custody. Candidate output is untrusted and never checker evidence. Lost replies require identity readback.
profile.required_proof: Pi/native protocol fixtures; launch failures; partial frames; wrong actual model; cancellation races; residual writable process and hostile output isolation.

profile.outcome: Replaceable admitted adapters execute bounded model work with actual model/process identity, stream custody, cancellation and retained result evidence.
profile.integrated_scenario: Run an admitted Pi/native fixture, collect bounded output/usage and reconcile the same assignment after a lost response.
profile.fault_and_benign: Wrong model, partial/oversized frame, hostile output, timeout or surviving writable child fails or remains pending; valid result retains provenance.
profile.complexity_boundary: No vendor assumptions in task ownership; adapter launch never grants broader access.

profile.focus: Process/workspace custody, hostile output, real model identity, cancellation and residual writable children.

tasks.intent: Define the first task and release contract
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T01 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: A real contained development task names inputs, acceptance, privacy, budget mode, pilot workload/window and measurable release targets. It can be expressed without an LLM or an inherited HEE packet set. Define loop limits, no-progress policy, criterion-to-verifier mapping and the minimal completion predicate before dispatch. Fix the initial module responsibilities, bidirectional boundary contracts and API/Unix-socket schema, with one state owner and no circular build dependencies. Freeze the minimal action IDs/envelope, error taxonomy, idempotency selector and state dimensions before the early CLI/UDS slice. Declare actual numeric resource/transport bounds during contract implementation.

tasks.intent: Implement the transactional task ledger
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T04 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Submission replay is idempotent; same key with different content conflicts; task/attempt/event updates commit together; migrations and consistent backup have failure tests. The first ledger includes atomic conservative work/verification reservations, effect uncertainty and cancellation intent. task.get can recover a lost admission reply by principal-scoped request key. Allocate event identity before immutable manifest creation; acceptance commits its reference with the outbox. Publish immutable artifacts crash-durably under a declared filesystem contract before committing their SQLite references; a completed write alone is insufficient. Use file/metadata synchronisation and atomic publication as required by that contract. Historical acceptance and current evidence availability are separate facts.

tasks.intent: Close one execute–verify–repair loop with completion evidence
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T06 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: A contained task uses the selected recipe and owned workspace, produces an artifact, runs an actual acceptance check and records result/cost. Worker end or exit zero alone cannot accept it. A failing candidate is repaired and reverified; exhausted and verifier-error cases stop truthfully. Acceptance and completion outbox event commit together with a criterion-to-evidence manifest bound to the actual candidate. Even this first loop requires a safe minimal budget gate and reserved verification allocation; unknown accounting cannot satisfy a hard ceiling. Rich cross-adapter reconciliation follows in T10. Terminal cancellation requires observed cleanup/effect reconciliation.

tasks.intent: Recover and cancel owned attempts
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T07 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Crashes before/after dispatch acknowledgement, stale generations, PID reuse, queued Pi messages and partial cleanup produce correct recoverable states without duplicate writes. Ambiguous external outcomes remain explicit. Cover restart at verification/evidence/acceptance boundaries; lease expiry alone cannot authorize reuse of a still-writable old workspace. Acceptance explicitly rejects any earlier committed cancellation intent, even before terminal cleanup. If acceptance committed first, later cancellation cannot rewrite history. Startup may reattach observation to a positively reconciled live attempt without redispatch. Restored ledger epochs cannot silently reuse prior event cursors.

tasks.intent: Account for whole-task cost and bounded fallback
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T10 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Concurrent reservations cannot exceed configured bounds; retries/checking/compaction are included; unknown usage is visible; hard-ceiling tasks reject incompatible accounting; fallback cannot cross privacy or tool constraints.

tasks.intent: Compare routing against a fixed-model baseline
tasks.route: Julia evaluation engineer + independent task reviewer
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T12 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Held-out representative tasks use the same acceptance method; failed/abandoned attempts enter cost totals; report uncertainty by class and review work. Retain a simple policy unless a challenger improves the declared tradeoff. Julia reports routing and cohort comparisons from the same immutable outcomes, with uncertainty and missingness. Include failed, cancelled and abandoned attempts and unknown usage at an explicit dataset cutoff; disclose exclusion and censoring policy.

tasks.intent: Add scoped lifecycle actions through systemd
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T14 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Only explicitly managed units can change state; dependencies and result readback are checked; stalled service, restart loop and coordinator restart cases do not create competing process owners.

tasks.intent: Qualify worker isolation and secret delivery
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T15 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Untrusted worker cannot read coordinator state/socket or unintended credentials; argv/env/cwd are explicit; resource and process-group cleanup are tested; trusted-host mode has an honest separate claim. Qualify isolation for candidate-controlled verification subprocesses, including build.rs, procedural macros, tests and Julia hooks. The trusted launcher/collector remains outside that execution domain; candidate code cannot modify protected fixtures, authoritative evidence, ledger/socket or unrelated secrets.

tasks.intent: Exercise the critical failure matrix
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T17 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Lost completion, stalled runtime, stale lease, duplicate submission, exhausted budget, provider failure and disk error each hit the intended boundary. Record exact build/config and limitations; do not substitute test count for outcome. Fabricated done, wrong-subject evidence, mid-check artifact mutation, broken verifier, repeated non-progress, failed parent integration and lost final notification cannot produce false accepted completion. Exercise partial/coalesced frames, slow API readers, stale event cursors, wrong socket/session and lost response after effect. Inject failures between artifact write, durability publication and acceptance commit under the declared filesystem contract. Missing, expired or corrupt evidence at later readback must report current unavailability while preserving the historical event; no fresh verification may be inferred. Fault experiments distinguish invalid fixtures, excluded cells and unmeasured gates. A formatting rejection that prevents the intended behavioral fault does not prove that behavioral detector works.

tasks.intent: Package and prove backup, upgrade and rollback
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T18 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Versioned artifact, dependencies and config are identifiable; login/reboot behaviour is observed; consistent backup restores tasks/artifacts; upgrade and schema-compatible rollback run on disposable state before installation. Before restoring a pre-upgrade database, preserve the failed/current ledger and reconcile post-backup operations, effects and usage. Use a disposable bounded qualification domain; a changed event epoch alone does not prevent replaying external effects erased by restore. Backup/restore and retention must preserve declared durability and unresolved evidence obligations. Retention policy states which accepted proof must remain retrievable; evidence loss is reported rather than silently rewriting acceptance or claiming current proof. Integration freshness reports include source additions/removals/changes; accepting an updated baseline is a separate versioned reconciliation, never an automatic consequence of discovery. Restore qualification compares the expected content/service inventory, includes an omitted-service control and independently reads back answering interfaces and residual processes in the disposable scope. File copying alone cannot prove restored operation; local recovery does not establish off-site disaster recovery.

tasks.intent: Run the constrained real-work pilot
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T19 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Under the concrete commissioning choice D07, run the Phase-1 workload/window; measure accepted work, total cost, rework, idle calls and incidents. Meet declared release targets or fix the observed gap without widening scope. Audit sampled criterion-to-evidence records and real repair loops; report false acceptance, verification error and completion-delivery failures.

tasks.intent: Release the scoped product and prune unnecessary machinery
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T20 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: A fresh operator can submit, inspect, cancel, recover and manage the declared services. Publish supported versions/limits and actual evidence. Remove duplicate status/procedure sources; advanced roadmap items remain optional. Pruning/update review keeps observed drift separate from the accepted baseline. Exact source anchors support presence/location claims only, not runtime behavior or compatibility.

tasks.intent: Establish the Rust and Julia quality contract
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T25 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Pinned format/lint/test recipes include pedantic Clippy, supported feature profiles, Rust doctests, locked Julia tests with explicit bounds checks, and honest case/skip counts. A deliberately bad fixture fails for the intended reason. Checks grow with each vertical slice; no blanket lint suppression. The verifier recipe separates trusted launch/collection from candidate-controlled compiler/build/test processes. Captured process exit status is an observation; candidate structured reports remain claims requiring recipe checks and independent expectations. Early trusted-host fixture tests must disclose that stronger hostile-code containment is not yet qualified. Qualify consequential gate discrimination on a passing baseline and an independently justified fault with the intended failure reason; include benign near-neighbors where false positives matter. Non-blocking authoring hooks do not satisfy required release gates.

tasks.intent: Define the threat model and security review contract
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T26 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Map task authority, context provenance, credentials, IPC, same-UID limits, isolation and trusted verifier ownership. Assign bounded negative cases and finding disposition. Confirm the selected security-model capability without granting extra execution authority. Include candidate-controlled build scripts, procedural macros, test binaries and Julia package hooks in the threat model; invoking them via a trusted verifier confers no collector authority.

tasks.intent: Close security findings against the integrated release
tasks.route: Security + verification threads, separate from finding implementer
tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T27 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
tasks.acceptance: Reproduce material findings, verify fixes and residual dispositions on the actual packaged candidate. Prompt injection, credential exposure, socket/method misuse, stale writers, fabricated evidence, dependency drift and resource exhaustion cannot produce false acceptance. Model review alone is not closure. In disposable qualified fixtures, candidate build/test code attempts to alter protected fixture, evidence and control paths. The boundary must refuse the effect and the independent collector must expose the attempt; an exit-zero candidate report cannot certify its own integrity. Security fault cases require a valid unmutated baseline and the intended observable refusal. Preserve unmeasured/excluded scope; one corpus with no unique catch does not justify removing a gate.

implementation_tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T02 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
implementation_tasks.acceptance: Fixture and later permitted smoke cases cover LF framing, model readback, usage, queued work, retry/end/settled ordering, cancellation and malformed/truncated records. Record the supported Rust/Pi protocol pair; no broad framework scaffold.

implementation_tasks.intent: Define common worker and plain inference contracts
implementation_tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T03 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
implementation_tasks.acceptance: Launch, observe, cancel and result semantics work for tool-capable and output-only models. Missing features return unsupported; normalisation retains provider-specific usage and actual identity.

implementation_tasks.intent: Build the model and agent roster
implementation_tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T05 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
implementation_tasks.acceptance: Profiles and instances are distinct; declared/effective capabilities and freshness are visible; disable prevents new work; importing a roster starts nothing; secrets remain references. SQLite owns admitted roster revisions. Reviewed TOML manifests are explicit bootstrap/import/export inputs through the same validated update authority: expected-absent creates, expected-revision updates. Invalid or stale import changes nothing. Test update/disable, restart and stale re-import; no admitted mutation is lost and disabled records remain disabled. Active attempts retain their pinned record snapshots.

implementation_tasks.intent: Build inspect-only service inventory and useful probes
implementation_tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T13 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
implementation_tasks.acceptance: Daemon, one-shot, library, remote endpoint and neural-operator records use appropriate observations. Unknown/stale readiness cannot become healthy; discovery claims no lifecycle ownership. Apply T05 admitted-revision and explicit import/export rules to service records. Test service update/disable, restart and stale/invalid import; observed inventory cannot overwrite effective authority or grant lifecycle control.

implementation_tasks.intent: Implement the bounded Rust–Julia analysis exchange
implementation_tasks.validation_cmd: Proposed, not implemented: habitat-engine-check case T21 --fixture-root <disposable-fixtures>
implementation_tasks.acceptance: An immutable attempt dataset produces a reproducible Julia report with dataset/schema identity. Missing data, nonfinite values, stale results, timeout and cancellation are explicit. Julia failure preserves the approved route and cannot mutate task ownership. Exercise the bidirectional contract corpus with independent expectations, numeric tolerances and explicit Julia bounds checks.

profile.surface: Rust verifier facade operating on protected fixtures and the exact candidate subject; evidence consumers are task/release admission.

operations.inputs: Acceptance revision, source/artifact subject, admitted fixture and toolchain identities
operations.outputs: Bounded verification plan with independent oracle and collector custody

operations.inputs: Exact execution outputs, profiles, case identities and diagnostics
operations.outputs: Per-criterion pass/fail/invalid/unmeasured observations with raw references

operations.inputs: Observation set, module standard and integration obligations
operations.outputs: Coverage/subject/diagnostic/assimilation/mutation gaps and candidate disposition

profile.errors_and_limits: Wrong-subject, zero-execution, skipped, stale and forged observations cannot pass. Baseline warnings/errors must be zero.
profile.effects_and_concurrency: Checker cannot accept its own task or trust worker-authored receipts. Protected output capture and tests are isolated from candidate write authority.
profile.required_proof: Forged result and fixture tamper detectors; wrong subject/profile; meaningful 50-case accounting; intended-fault plus benign mirror; full-standard collector qualification remains future work.

profile.outcome: Acceptance checks have qualified detectors and complete exact-subject evidence; forged, empty, stale or wrong-profile proof cannot become success.
profile.integrated_scenario: A known faulty candidate fails for the intended reason, its benign mirror passes, and a repaired integrated candidate is reverified against the same criteria.
profile.fault_and_benign: Mutate fixture identity, case inventory, profile, producer status or raw log; reject each without accepting an aggregate count.
profile.complexity_boundary: The full admission collector must be implemented and qualified before this module is accepted; no self-declared trust.

profile.focus: Forged evidence, compromised fixtures, invalid denominator and independent verifier/collector custody.
profile.fault_and_benign: Mutate fixture identity, case inventory, profile, producer status or raw log; reject each without accepting an aggregate count.

limitations: Record consistency is not producer authentication, runtime certification or task acceptance.
Only declared files/checks are covered; omitted transitive inputs and mandatory criteria require owner review.
Future timestamps are unqualified; no age expiry or current deployment health is inferred.

modules.owns: Attempt reconciliation, ambiguity and cleanup policy

flows.request_context: Persisted active attempts and observed process/session identities
